label: BW-style / CLI-adapted

rubric_scores.evidence: The renovation setting and far-right window relationship are recognizable, but the enclosure is substantially broader and shallower than the required narrow, deep room.
Repeated brown studs occupy the left side, but their backing is a plain continuous surface without visible reddish-brown coursed brick.
The inset far-wall window has an off-white perimeter frame and clearly stacked upper and lower sash regions.
The ladder has paired rails, repeated steps and an open folding structure near the window, but appears white and nonmetallic and stands independently without upper wall-associated support.
A light rectangular electrical box is mounted on the near-left framing with a connected conduit descending toward the floor.
Numerous wooden strips concentrate in the foreground, but the masonry debris consists of sparse, regular rectangular chips rather than a field of irregular broken masonry.

Lower horizontal slats are present, but the far wall is uniformly smooth and neatly coursed rather than rough and patchy. The ladder lacks a convincing aluminum surface, and exposed floor areas are uniformly clean.
Warm illumination and a concentrated bright high-left work light establish the intended atmosphere while leaving the scene elements readable.

The original PNG decodes successfully and shows the entrance-facing composition with the principal elements together. The opened Blender project contains separate editable meshes, assigned materials, three lights and an active authored camera whose rerender matches the delivered composition.

dimension_scores.evidence: Main objects and their general arrangement correspond, but room proportions, stripped masonry and construction wear differ substantially.
Fixtures and ladder form coherent assemblies with plausible general support; some wooden strips appear suspended slightly above the floor or loosely intersect their pile.
Brown timber, pale window framing and blue panes preserve the broad palette, but white ladder surfaces and uniform beige masonry weaken correspondence.
Regular primitive geometry, pristine surfaces, rectangular rubble and visible render noise make the scene read as a simplified model.
Left framing and electrical box, rear window, right-side ladder and foreground wood pile retain their broad relationships; enclosure depth and width are less faithful.
Objects remain recognizable, but the room feels overly broad and tall, with a narrow ladder and unusually elongated brick courses.
Warm localized lighting and directional shadows work well, but wood, masonry and ladder surfaces lack convincing material-specific character.

Window, ladder, repeated studs, electrical box, conduit, work light and both debris categories are present. Left-side exposed brick and substantial demolition rubble are missing or inadequately represented.

same_model_bias_limit: Research and independent judge use Astra; separate sessions do not establish human independence.
